parsed.why: Most Protective tier: no facility ban, GI hate-crime and accommodation protections, healthcare shield law. Only the hostile national border/document screening and custody regime, which every division shares, holds it below Reduced Risk.

Unique law criminalising restroom/changing-room use in all public-facing businesses, misdemeanour up to a year, suit pending. A universal-exposure facility offence reaching every outed visitor, so materially below the parent line.

Facility law enforced within days: troopers checking ID at women's restrooms, school-district inquiry, Do Not Travel tier, binary definition act barring marker changes, documented denial of prison care. State-directed universal exposure plus active enforcement.

School facility ban plus executive order applying birth-sex rules to state-owned restrooms and changing rooms; marker changes foreclosed; care bans reaching adults in public facilities; no GI hate-crime coverage. Not criminalised for adults generally, so above dossiers 2 and 3.

2016 bathroom law repealed; no current statute barring facility use or criminalising it, though a 2025 bill revives the question and documents now must retain original sex. Open question rather than known exposure; no statewide GI protections or bias-crime recourse.
